hook.text: Satellites can now detect a single cleared hectare of forest within 24 hours.

buildup.text: Global Forest Watch provides free, real-time deforestation alerts to anyone with internet.

discovery.text: AI analyzes thousands of satellite images daily, flagging suspicious changes automatically.

twist.text: The data shows deforestation accelerating even in countries that promised to stop it.

climax.text: Transparency doesn't automatically lead to action, but it makes denial impossible.

punchline.text: Every tree that falls is now visible from space.

quiz.question: What is Global Forest Watch?
options: A free platform providing real-time deforestation alerts
A government agency that plants trees

details.summary: Satellite monitoring systems like Global Forest Watch track deforestation in near-real time using radar and optical imagery, sending alerts within days of clearing. This technology has transformed accountability by making forest loss visible to anyone with internet access.
details.whyItMatters: Satellite monitoring removes the excuse of not knowing where deforestation happens. Real-time data enables rapid response by authorities, NGOs, and companies.
takeaways: Global Forest Watch provides free deforestation alerts within days
Radar works through clouds, critical for monitoring tropical forests
Satellite data has revealed deforestation in supposedly protected areas

faq.question: How accurate is satellite deforestation monitoring?
faq.answer: Modern systems detect clearing as small as 0.5 hectares with high accuracy. Cloud-piercing radar ensures continuous monitoring in tropical regions. However, degradation from selective logging is harder to detect than outright clearing.

faq.question: Does satellite monitoring actually reduce deforestation?
faq.answer: Studies show that combining alerts with on-the-ground enforcement reduces illegal clearing by 30 to 50 percent. Monitoring alone is necessary but not sufficient; it must be paired with political will and legal consequences to be effective.
